facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old man
12-year history of perianal fistula
recent mucinous discharge, pain, and perianal induration
incision and drainage of a recurrent perianal abscess
two indurated, ulcerative lesions each 7 cm in diameter
three external fistula openings around the anus
no inguinal lymphadenopathy
Upper endoscopy was unremarkable
internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line
otherwise normal mucosa in the rectum and colon
well-defined mass at the level of the anorectal junction extending into the right ischiorectal fossa
Histological examination of a biopsy specimen from the indurated area revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma

concepts.why: The patient's biopsy specimen revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, and the presence of a well-defined mass at the anorectal junction supports this diagnosis.
The patient has a 12-year history of perianal fistula and recent findings of external fistula openings around the anus.
The patient had a history of incision and drainage of a recurrent perianal abscess, which is consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient's biopsy specimen revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, which is a type of anal cancer.
The patient's biopsy specimen revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, which can also occur in the rectum.

aliases: Cancer of the Colon and Rectum

concepts.why: The patient has a history of perianal fistula and recent findings of external fistula openings around the anus, which are consistent with anorectal disease.
The patient's biopsy specimen revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, which is a type of gastrointestinal cancer.
It explains the presence of two indurated, ulcerative lesions each 7 cm in diameter.

rationales.F03: Mucinous discharge and perianal induration suggest anorectal disease
rationales.F04: History of perianal abscess increases likelihood of anorectal disease
rationales.F05: Indurated lesions are highly suggestive of malignancy
rationales.F06: External fistula openings are common in anorectal disease
rationales.F07: Absence of inguinal lymphadenopathy does not rule out malignancy
rationales.F08: Normal upper endoscopy does not rule out anorectal disease
rationales.F09: Internal fistula opening is consistent with anorectal disease
rationales.F10: Normal mucosa in rectum and colon does not rule out anorectal disease
rationales.F11: Mass at anorectal junction is highly suggestive of malignancy
rationales.F12: Mucinous adenocarcinoma is a specific diagnosis

frontier_selector.rationale: Histological examination of a biopsy specimen from the indurated area revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, which directly supports Mucinous Adenocarcinoma of the Anus, and the location at the anorectal junction is more specific to this diagnosis than the broader Anal Cancer.
